overview: Sigma 4.11's Disabler is a five-mode packet bypass module driven from a single EventUpdate plus EventPacket handler. The registered modes are Hypixel (default), Faithful, Erisium, SagePvP and ColdNetwork; the ViperMC branches in onEnable and onEvent are dead code because ViperMC is never registered in the Options array. Hypixel mode fires a triple C04 ground-claim sequence on enable, then cancels every outgoing C03 for up to five seconds while zeroing motion and enabling noClip, ending when the next S08 teleport arrives; the S08 is also rewritten in place with the local yaw and pitch. Faithful cancels every outgoing C00 keepalive. Erisium parks the keepalive echo and re-sends the same key 1500ms later. SagePvP and ColdNetwork cancel accepted window-0 C0F confirmations. The C0A, C17, S02, ItemBook and ByteBuf imports are never used.

sections.h: Mode dispatch and the dead ViperMC branch
sections.p: The MODE setting is an Options object over the five registered strings, and the handler re-reads the selection whenever it changes. ViperMC appears only as equality tests in onEnable and onEvent: the 10-packet C04 burst (y plus or minus 0.2 for indexes outside 2..8, all onGround true, queued through addToSendQueue) and the y-plus-0.4 lift after a 3000ms timer can never execute because no setting value produces the ViperMC string. The mode string is also mirrored to the module suffix on every event.

On enable, while grounded and vertically collided, the mode sends a C04PacketPlayerPosition at the current y with onGround true, then a second at y plus 0.16 and a third at y plus 0.07, all through sendPacketNoEvent; the pre-event path repeats the same triple each time the ground gate passes while the watchdog flag is clear. After the claims land, watchdog is set: every outgoing C03PacketPlayer is cancelled for up to five seconds, the local motion and jumpMovementFactor are zeroed, noClip is enabled and the local onGround flag is forced false. The window closes when the next S08PacketPlayerPosLook arrives, which the handler rewrites in place with the current yaw and pitch before disabling the module with the 'you can do what you want for 5s' notice. During the freeze the client keeps its local physics (noClip lets the player walk through blocks) while the server sees no movement at all.

Faithful cancels every outgoing C00PacketKeepAlive, so the server never receives a keepalive echo. Erisium instead parks the echo: each incoming S00PacketKeepAlive stores its key and arms the flag, the outgoing C00 with that key is cancelled, and 1500ms later (a Timer reset on every S00) a fresh C00PacketKeepAlive carrying the same key is sent through sendPacketNoEvent. SagePvP and ColdNetwork cancel every C0FPacketConfirmTransaction whose window id is 0 and accepted flag is true, so inventory confirmations never reach the server. The module also carries a Faithful relog notice and an Erisium state reset when the client is at tick 1.

files.label: Disabler.java
files.explanation: The complete module. The EventUpdate pre handler runs the movement side (Hypixel triple C04 claims, the watchdog state, the dead ViperMC burst, the Erisium keepalive release) and the EventPacket pre handler runs the packet side (C03 cancel while watchdog, S08 yaw and pitch rewrite, S00 key capture, C00 cancel or park, C0F cancel). The mode selection is a plain Options setting over the five mode strings. The 188-line file is self-contained: the C0A, C17, S02, ItemBook and ByteBuf imports are unused, and all packet work uses sendPacketNoEvent or addToSendQueue through the vanilla queue.

countering.label: KeepAliveFrequency (keepalive ledger)
countering.explanation: NoCheatPlus replaces vanilla's accept-any-echo keepalive model with an id ledger. The ProtocolLib KeepAliveAdapter records every outgoing S00 id into NetData.keepAliveRequests, pruned after 30000ms and capped at 40 pending, and each incoming C00 is matched against that list: a reply with a matching pending request sets the expected-response guard and bails, while a reply with no pending request or a duplicate id is counted. Every C00 is timestamped into an ActionFrequency(20, 1000), and the check flags when the newest bucket scores above 1f (more than one reply in the same second), on duplicate ids, or on unexpected replies. The Erisium mode's single 1500ms-delayed echo keeps the original key, so it still matches its pending request inside the 30-second window and the check bails: the delayed-echo trick passes by design at this rate, and a burst of several parked echoes released together would be what trips the bucket. The Faithful blanket cancel produces no replies at all, which starves the ledger entirely: the honest pressure on that mode is the server's own keepalive timeout, not this check.

countering.label: NegativeTimer (delayed-packet timeline)
countering.explanation: Grim's NegativeTimer flags a client whose movement delivery runs slower than the expected 20 ticks per second. The base Timer adds 50ms of balance per received movement packet, anchors the balance to real time, and NegativeTimer's prediction handler flags once real time outruns the balance by the drift (default 1200ms), with the balance clamped to the player's transaction-derived clock minus drift. The check is designed around a drip, not a freeze: the standing-still exemption resets the balance whenever no point-three movement has occurred recently, and the clamp forgives gaps by construction, so the Hypixel mode's total C03 cancellation for up to five seconds is absorbed rather than flagged. The freeze is nevertheless the mode's real liability: it exists to hide local movement, and any anticheat that ties movement to the transaction stream (which keeps flowing while C03s are cancelled) sees the client clock advance while the position stream stands still. The check is an honest boundary here: it bites sustained slow delivery of a still-flowing stream, which is the drip shape, not Sigma's hard freeze.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (movement physics envelope)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly rebuilds the physics envelope from the world and ignores packet ground claims. The Hypixel mode's triple C04 sequence (y, y plus 0.16, y plus 0.07, all with onGround true) presents a net grounded ascent of 0.07 blocks: vDistRel only accepts zero-y moves on ground, jumps, steps and riptide launches, and the block cache at minY minus yOnGround says the claimed height is air, so the grounded claim fails on the first packet. The 0.16 intermediate claim is a 0.16 vertical delta in a single move, far above the vertical allowance for a grounded tick. The freeze is where the envelope bites hardest: after up to five seconds with no position updates, the first C03 after the S08 disables the module claims a position the client reached by walking locally with noClip, and the server-side distance from the frozen position exceeds both the horizontal and vertical allowances, producing a violation of hundreds and an immediate set-back. The yaw and pitch rewrite on S08 does not help: the server applies the teleport and re-anchors its tracking, so the resume gap is measured from the teleported location either way.
